My name is not important, but let me tell you how I think about this year.

I have 12 mu of land. I split it like I always do — 8 mu for wheat then maize after, and 4 mu for cotton. Cotton is more work but the price has been decent the last two years, and my daughter-in-law helps at picking time.

For my wheat, I plant in October. I use improved seed, "Jimai 22" or whatever the agro-shop in town has that year — my neighbors all use it and get 450 to 500 jin per mu. Before planting I plough the land and spread my base fertilizer: one bag of compound fertilizer (45% total, 15-15-15) per mu, that's 50 jin. Then at green-up in spring I top-dress with urea, about 30 jin per mu. That comes to roughly 20 kg of nitrogen per mu total when I count both. I irrigate at green-up, at jointing, and at grain-filling — three times. If spring is very dry I add one more. I spray twice, once for aphids, once for scab if the weather turns wet at flowering.

For my summer maize after wheat, I plant hybrid seed — "Zhengdan 958" type. I do not plough, I just plant directly into the wheat stubble with the seed drill the machine man brings. At the big-trumpet stage I side-dress urea, about 35 jin per mu. I give compound fertilizer 30 jin at planting. That is around 18-20 kg N per mu. I irrigate once at the big-trumpet stage, twice if no rain. Pesticide once for borer.

For my 4 mu cotton, this is where I spend more. I plough deep in early spring, use one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu as base — cotton eats a lot. Then I top-dress urea 25 jin at bud stage and another 20 jin at flowering. Cotton needs spraying many times for bollworm and aphid — I do 6 or 7 sprays, that is just how it is. Irrigate 3 times if the well allows. I expect about 250 jin of seed cotton per mu. Less than when I was younger, but my back cannot do what it used to.

I do not change much from last year. My neighbors do the same. Fertilizer is expensive but short harvest is worse.
